## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)
*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and SuttaCentral data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*
The *Piṭṭhadhītalikapetavatthu* (Pv 4, also referenced as Pv 1.4), translated as "Advice to a Daughter" or "Ghost Story of the Biscuit Doll", is a verse narrative within the *Petavatthu* collection [SuttaCentral; Sayers 2008; Sayers 2013]. The text addresses the theme of how the living can help their departed relatives [SuttaCentral]. In the narrative, the Buddha advocates ancestor propitiation, instructing a follower to make generous offerings on behalf of those who have died (*pubbapete*), as well as to household deities and the four world-guardian kings [Sayers 2008; Sayers 2013]. In morphological studies of canonical Pali, verse 4.5 of the text has been cited as a rare instance attesting both a *gacch-* and a *ganch-* aorist stem [Kingsbury 2002].
No cross-language parallels are recorded on SuttaCentral, and DharmaNexus identifies no cross-language alignments scoring 10 or higher [SuttaCentral; DharmaNexus]. DharmaNexus does, however, identify internal Pali text reuse across three passages shared with the commentary, the *Petavatthu-aṭṭhakathā*, the longest segment extending through §1.1–4.4 [DharmaNexus]. Four translations across four languages are indexed on SuttaCentral [SuttaCentral].
**Parallels and text reuse**

- Text reuse within the Pali corpus (DharmaNexus): Petavatthu-aṭṭhakathā (Atk S0507a) (§1.1–4.4 ↔ §101–112)
